title: Co-op Legal Services using AI to rate workers' phone calls to customers
key_facts: Co-op Legal Services uses AI models to record, analyse and give a percentage score to phone calls between its advisers and customers seeking advice on probate, wills and estates.
A model from OpenAI has been trained to assess more than 50 discrete aspects of each call and give managers pass and fail scores.
A whistleblower calls the system 'oppressive and dystopian'; one worker says the AI can monitor their work for several hours a day.
The monitoring was introduced in the last couple of months for dozens of legal services staff and is used in part to identify ways to boost sales performance.
The Co-op says the AI is a support tool, not a decision-maker, and that it helps ensure clients receive empathetic expert guidance.
The Communication Workers Union says AI monitoring can diminish sensible workplace practices, and the ILO warned about psychosocial risks of AI monitoring this year.
quote_evidence: The AI monitoring is understood to have been introduced in the last couple of months into the work of dozens of legal services staff.
AI is sold as the solution to every problem, but examples like this make it clear that it can diminish sensible workplace practices and intensify working lives for no reason,
why_it_matters_hint: AI call scoring is spreading into customer-facing legal work, with staff saying it feels like constant surveillance.
